```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

# The walkthrough runs the CTAS engine, so it needs the gsm framework and the
# SDTM test data. Chunks are skipped rather than failed when they are missing,
# so the vignette still builds on a minimal machine.
bRun <- all(vapply(
  c("gsm.core", "gsm.mapping", "gsm.reporting", "pharmaversesdtm", "workr"),
  requireNamespace,
  logical(1),
  quietly = TRUE
))

knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = bRun)
```

`gsm.ctas` runs the [ctas](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctas) anomaly
detection engine inside the [gsm](https://github.com/Gilead-BioStats/gsm.core)
workflow framework, so that CTAS site scores appear alongside the usual KRIs in
a standard gsm site report.

This vignette walks the whole path -- SDTM domains in, rendered KRI report out
-- and then covers the two things most users will want to change: the
thresholds, and the set of metrics.

## Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("IMPALA-Consortium/gsm.ctas")
```

The `ctas` engine and the gsm framework packages are declared in `Remotes` and
are installed along with it.

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(gsm.ctas)
```

## The shape of the pipeline

gsm is a YAML-driven engine: each layer is a directory of workflow files, and
`RunWorkflows()` executes them in order.

```
lRaw --Ingest--> lIngest --1_mappings--> lMapped --2_metrics--> lAnalysis
     --3_reporting--> Reporting_* --4_modules--> HTML report
```

`gsm.ctas` ships all four layers in `inst/workflow/`:

| Layer | Contents |
|---|---|
| `1_mappings` | `DM`, `VS`, `LB`, `SITE`, `STUDY`, plus `CTAS_Input` -> `CTAS_SiteScores` -> `CTAS_Detail` |
| `2_metrics` | `ctas0001`-`ctas0011`, one per parameter family x CTAS feature |
| `3_reporting` | `Groups`, `Metrics`, `Results`, `Bounds` |
| `4_modules` | `report_kri_site` |

The important structural point: CTAS is an *all-metrics-at-once* engine. One
`ctas::process_a_study()` call scores every timeseries x feature x site, so it
runs **once**, in `1_mappings/CTAS_SiteScores.yaml`, and each metric workflow
merely filters the shared `Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores` object down to one parameter
family and one feature.

## Input data

`pharmaversesdtm` provides the SDTM domains. The example is cut down to six
sites and a handful of tests to keep the engine fast.

```{r data}
vSites <- sort(unique(pharmaversesdtm::dm$SITEID))[1:6]

dfDM <- pharmaversesdtm::dm[pharmaversesdtm::dm$SITEID %in% vSites, ]
dfVS <- pharmaversesdtm::vs[
  pharmaversesdtm::vs$USUBJID %in% dfDM$USUBJID &
    pharmaversesdtm::vs$VSTESTCD %in% c("SYSBP", "DIABP", "PULSE"),
]
dfLB <- pharmaversesdtm::lb[
  pharmaversesdtm::lb$USUBJID %in% dfDM$USUBJID &
    pharmaversesdtm::lb$LBTESTCD %in% c("ALB", "BILI", "CREAT"),
]

lRaw <- list(
  Raw_DM = as.data.frame(dfDM),
  Raw_VS = as.data.frame(dfVS),
  Raw_LB = as.data.frame(dfLB)
)
```

## 1. Mapping and the CTAS run

```{r mappings}
lMappingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/1_mappings", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lIngest <- gsm.mapping::Ingest(
  lRaw,
  gsm.mapping::CombineSpecs(lMappingWorkflows)
)

# CTAS emits `cor()` "standard deviation is zero" warnings for flat series.
# They are genuine data-quality signal, so the package does not suppress them;
# only this vignette does.
lMapped <- suppressWarnings(
  gsm.core::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = lMappingWorkflows, lData = lIngest)
)

names(lMapped)
```

Labs are mapped **twice** from the same domain, because the two questions are
different:

* `Input_Range()` -> `LB_NORM_*` -- do a site's *values* deviate, once the
  reference range has made different tests comparable?
* `Input_Missing()` -> `LB_MISS_*` -- does its *completeness* deviate? The
  value-based input drops missing results, so it is structurally blind to this.

`Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores` is the shared result: one row per timeseries x feature
x site, carrying the identifiers needed to tell the families apart.

```{r scores}
utils::head(lMapped$Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores, 3)

unique(lMapped$Mapped_CTAS_SiteScores[
  , c("parameter_category_1", "parameter_category_3")
])
```

The mapping functions also work directly, outside a workflow:

```{r direct}
lInput <- Combine_CTAS_Input(
  dfVS = Input_Numeric(
    dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_VS,
    strSubjectCol = "USUBJID",
    strTestCDCol = "VSTESTCD",
    strTestCol = "VSTEST",
    strValueCol = "VSSTRESN",
    strVisitCol = "VISIT",
    strVisitNumCol = "VISITNUM",
    strCategory = "Vital Signs",
    strPrefix = "VS"
  ),
  dfSubjects = Input_Subjects(
    dfDM = lMapped$Mapped_DM,
    strSubjectCol = "USUBJID",
    strSiteCol = "SITEID",
    strCountryCol = "COUNTRY"
  )
)

names(lInput)
```

## 2. Metrics

Each metric filters the shared scores to one family and one feature, then
aggregates timeseries into the gsm `Analysis_Analyzed` contract.

```{r metrics}
lMetricWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/2_metrics", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lAnalysis <- gsm.core::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows,
  lData = lMapped
)

utils::head(lAnalysis$Analysis_ctas0001$Analysis_Flagged)
```

The aggregation is:

| gsm field | CTAS source |
|---|---|
| `GroupID` | `site_scores$site` |
| `Numerator` | timeseries with `trigger == "Further Evaluation"` |
| `Denominator` | timeseries evaluated for that group x feature |
| `Metric` | `Numerator / Denominator` |
| `Score` | `max(fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp)` |

Flagging is **one-sided** (`0`/`1`/`2`): $-\log_{10}p$ is unsigned, so it says
that a site differs, not in which direction.

`Denominator` counts *timeseries*, not participants and not tests -- CTAS
autogenerates a timeseries per timepoint combination, so the lab families
contribute more of them than vital signs do.

## 3-4. Reporting and the KRI report

```{r reporting}
lReportingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/3_reporting", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lReporting <- gsm.core::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lReportingWorkflows,
  lData = c(
    lMapped,
    list(lAnalyzed = lAnalysis, lWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows)
  )
)

names(lReporting)
```

There is deliberately no `Reporting_Input`. CTAS has no subject-level
numerator/denominator -- each subject contributes a whole timeseries and the
statistic is computed on a distribution -- so synthesising one would be a
fiction that renders misleadingly. The stock `gsm.kri` site report does not need
one.

```{r report, eval = FALSE}
lModuleWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/4_modules", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

workr::RunWorkflows(lModuleWorkflows, lReporting)
```

The module drops the stock scatter plot via `DropChart()`. That chart plots
`Denominator` against `Numerator`, which suits a rate metric where the
denominator is exposure; here it is a coverage count, near-identical across
sites, so the points collapse onto one x position. The bar chart and KRI table
carry the same information on the $-\log_{10}p$ scale the metric is actually
defined on.

## Customising thresholds

Thresholds are exposed the gsm-native way, through `meta` and `ParseThreshold`.
Edit the metric YAML -- no code change, no fork:

```yaml
meta:
  Threshold: 0.842, 2.326   # flagging cut points, -log10(p) scale
  TriggerHigh: 2.326        # timeseries -> "Further Evaluation"
  TriggerLow: 0.842         # timeseries -> "Watch List"
```

`TriggerHigh` / `TriggerLow` classify *timeseries*, feeding `Numerator`.
`Threshold` classifies *groups*, feeding `Flag`. The same numbers, different
jobs.

The defaults `2.326` and `0.842` are one-sided normal z-quantiles (99% and 80%)
applied to a $-\log_{10}p$ scale, where they correspond to $p \approx 0.0047$
and $p \approx 0.144$. They are adopted from operational experience for
consistency with existing CTAS review, and documented here rather than silently
inherited.

To use your own workflows, copy the shipped directory and point
`MakeWorkflowList()` at the copy:

```{r custom, eval = FALSE}
lMyMetrics <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = "my_workflows/2_metrics",
  strPackage = NULL
)
```

## Adding a metric

A new metric is a YAML file, not a function. Copy `ctas0001.yaml` and change a
few `meta` fields:

```yaml
meta:
  ID: ctas0012
  Metric: CTAS Labs Missingness Autocorrelation
  Feature: autocorr               # a ctas timeseries feature
  Domain: "Labs"                  # parameter_category_1
  Transformation: "ratio_missing" # parameter_category_3
```

`Domain` and `Transformation` are required **together**, and `Summarize_CTAS()`
errors if only one is supplied. Neither identifies a family alone:

| | `Domain` | `Transformation` |
|---|---|---|
| `VS_*` | `Vital Signs` | `numeric` |
| `LB_NORM_*` | `Labs` | `range_normalized` |
| `LB_MISS_*` | `Labs` | `ratio_missing` |

A selector matching nothing is an error rather than an empty result: zero
timeseries would render every site as unevaluated, which is indistinguishable
from a genuinely absent domain.

To score a feature the shipped workflows do not compute, add it to `Features`
in `1_mappings/CTAS_SiteScores.yaml` as well.

## Drill-down: handing off to ctasapp

Aggregation collapses many timeseries into one row per site. The timeseries
detail is retained separately for the `ctasapp` dashboard, which is the tool for
investigating a signal that the gsm report has detected.

```{r detail}
lDetail <- lMapped$Mapped_CTAS_Detail
vapply(lDetail, nrow, numeric(1))
```

`Results` is the site scores unchanged; `Input` is the analysed series joined to
site and parameter labels; `Untransformed` holds the original values, so a lab
result can be shown in its own units next to the range-normalised value that was
actually analysed. Write them out for upload with:

```{r write, eval = FALSE}
Write_CTAS_Detail(lDetail, strPath = "ctas_detail", strFormat = "csv")
```

`parquet` is available via `Suggests: arrow`, and is worth using for deployment
-- `Input` is one row per subject x parameter x timepoint and grows quickly.
